author: Shurtz, Ammon; Richardson, Christian; Richardson, Stephen D.
title: MekongPhon: A Large-Scale Parallel IPA Corpus for Lao and Khmer
scope: Authors explicitly state that all data, code and pretrained models are publicly released to support future research and development (ACL Anthology record, abstract); ClippyFirst uses the pinned corpus for non-redistributive research, rule-discovery and comparative diagnostics. Paper reports 367,388 Lao orthography–IPA sentence pairs and a 6,039-entry seed lexicon derived from Kerr (1972), with a two-author 500-entry review (97.2% sample accuracy; reviewers are proficient L2 speakers, not native speakers). Pinned GitHub snapshot f80f6c1840c4818b51e05f2e00cded4701a5b662 contains 6,319 lexicon rows (6,316 unique spellings), 6,219 train rows (lao_train.csv SHA-256 2d0f68989009620980ced3386f11a640e6167404308eeb6a79efc52bc8e40ee0) and 100 eval rows; three duplicate spellings occur in train and there is no train/eval overlap. Sentence pairs are generated by longest-match trie lookup over OPUS text (NLLB/Paracrawl/OpenSubtitles); held-out evaluation is dictionary-seeded, not independent sentence transcription or ClippyFirst gold. The current ClippyFirst diagnostic consumes only the word-level seed-lexicon train split, not OPUS-derived sentence pairs; The upstream snapshot's missing root LICENSE remains a provenance fact. Independent reuse of SEAlang/OPUS outside MekongPhon remains governed by their own terms. The repository owner confirms full rights for all MekongPhon components in the authorized project use; this supersedes the preliminary UNKNOWN status and is not an independent legal opinion.

author: Ashby, Lucas F. E. et al.
title: Results of the Second SIGMORPHON Shared Task on Multilingual Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion
scope: Official 2021 task results and language inventory; Lao is not an official target language. Methodological comparator only.

author: Zhu, Jian; Zhang, Cong; Jurgens, David
title: ByT5 model for massively multilingual grapheme-to-phoneme conversion
scope: Interspeech 2022; multilingual ByT5 G2P, code and model release at https://github.com/lingjzhu/CharsiuG2P. At inspected commit 0c929390759fb94f8ecdfc05cc0bc5f2ff2dc0f4, sources/info/wikipron/lao_laoo_broad_info.txt points to CUNY-CL WikiPron lao_laoo_broad.tsv and declares Apache-2.0 for that source metadata. A recursive inspection of the same commit's full tree found no Lao file in data/train, data/dev or data/test and no Lao entry in the model's checked-in split inventories; Khmer is present. Therefore the presence of Lao source metadata does not establish Lao model training or evaluation, and CharsiuG2P is not currently a supervised Lao benchmark candidate on this revision.

author: Osatananda, Varisa
title: Tone in Vientiane Lao
scope: One Vientiane variety in Vientiane Prefecture; five lexical tones, final stress, and an analysis in which each syllable has underlying lexical tone rather than tone being mechanically derived by orthographic rules. Important competing analysis and dialect-specific caution; not a replacement rule table for the project's declared Vientiane profile.

author: Phissamay, Phonpasit; Dalolay, Valaxay; Chanhsililath, Chitaphone; Silimasak, Oulaiphone; Hussain, Sarmad; Durrani, Nadir
title: Syllabification of Lao Script for Line Breaking
scope: Working Papers 2004–2007, pp. 291–296; reports a rule-based orthographic syllable identification technique with more than 98% results, but the accessible paper does not establish a reproducible benchmark split or a pronunciation evaluation. It targets line breaking, not lexical word segmentation or IPA accuracy. Used as structural comparison only.

author: Phatthiyaphaibun, Wannaphong
title: LaoNLP: Lao language Natural Language Processing
scope: Open-source Lao NLP toolkit. Its syllable tokenizer documents example segmentation for ພາສາລາວໃນປັດຈຸບັນ and implements a regex model based on Phissamay et al.; package code is Apache-2.0. The bundled lao-eng-dictionary.csv has a separate explicit MIT notice from the E-Government Center, Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications of Laos. Neither the tokenizer nor dictionary is IPA gold.

author: E-Government Center, Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications of Laos
title: Lao-English dictionary dataset bundled with LaoNLP
scope: CSV inspected at immutable upstream commit a914f64e38ff24d67d32e37db40dad5c368ea602; blob SHA-1 ded14c7770becfd5c6946c6c1ce75a7dfc4d564c. Schema ID,LaoWord,English,Pronunciation,Type; 51,257 records. Quote-aware audit: 21 exact repeated header rows plus 3 header-like malformed rows (two misspell Pronunciation; one omits LaoWord), 3 ID-only rows, 35,078 distinct non-header LaoWord forms, 11,195 forms with multiple rows, 36 blank Type values, and 7 blank Pronunciation values (3 are ID-only rows). Pronunciation is Latin romanization, not IPA. Mixed phrases and inconsistent Type values mean this is not lexical-boundary gold. Not imported into runtime. Preserve separate MIT notice if redistributed.

author: Ylönen, Tatu; Wiktionary contributors
title: Machine-readable Lao dictionary extracted from English Wiktionary
scope: Snapshot extracted 2026-10-30 from enwiktionary dump 2026-10-01 using Wiktextract 19f9a30 and 6f96ddf; index reports 2,378 distinct word forms and a 5.2 MB postprocessed JSONL. IPA includes Vientiane and Luang Prabang variants. Exact raw wikitext revisions inspected for four pages explicitly call {{lo-pron}}: ກະດານ oldid 66396667; ການແປ 66459544; ຂໍກະແຈ 68829138; ຝົນ 85069045. Generator pinned to Module:lo-pron oldid 88555975 (2025-12-13), Template:lo-pron oldid 79053402 (2024-04-27), docs oldid 76254409 (2023-10-03). Processed sounds records do not retain source template invocation. Four-page sample proves generated IPA is present, not the corpus-wide proportion. Secondary diagnostic only, not independent gold. Underlying Wiktionary text CC BY-SA 4.0/GFDL; retain attribution/share-alike obligations.

author: Wiktionary contributors
title: Module:lo-pron and Template:lo-pron source revisions
scope: Exact Module:lo-pron raw source pinned at oldid 88555975 (2025-12-13T03:19:42Z); Template:lo-pron raw source at oldid 79053402 (2024-04-27T13:31:09Z); documentation at oldid 76254409 (2023-10-03T00:29:37Z). Module maps Lao initials, vowels, finals and Vientiane/Luang Prabang tone classes to IPA, then emits IPA through Module:IPA. Exact source entry revisions 66396667, 66459544, 68829138 and 85069045 invoke {{lo-pron}}. These four entries therefore have generated, not manually typed, IPA. Sample only; do not infer every Lao IPA page uses this template. Module dependencies such as Module:IPA and Module:rhymes are separate and can evolve; any full reproducible execution snapshot must pin their revisions too.

author: Lew, S.
title: A linguistic analysis of the Lao writing system and its suitability for minority language orthographies
scope: Writing Systems Research, pp. 25–40. Analyzes Lao grapheme–phoneme correspondences and orthographic structure; emphasizes dialectal differences in lexicon, vowels and especially tone. Useful for script-to-phoneme architecture, not an independent word-level IPA corpus.

author: Lao Language Specific Peculiarities document authors
title: Language Specific Peculiarities Document for Lao as Spoken in Laos 1. Dialects
scope: Documents major Lao dialect differences in pronunciation and tone; notes that ໃ and ໄ are pronounced the same in Vientiane but differently in Luang Prabang. Secondary language-resource profile; use for dialect boundary checks, not as a complete phonological grammar.

author: Enfield, N. J.
title: Word in Lao
scope: Describes syllables grouped into feet; each foot includes one stressed syllable bearing contrastive tone plus one or more unstressed phonologically dependent syllables. Grammatical-word and phonological-word boundaries do not always coincide. Useful for phrase/word segmentation caution, not a simple grapheme-level rule.

author: Davis, Garry W.
title: The Story of Lao r
scope: Discusses historical grapheme ຣ and loss of /r/: historical /r/ became /h/ under some conditions and /l/ elsewhere, and clusters were lost; loans from Pali-Sanskrit, Khmer and Thai complicate modern spellings. Supports conservative lexeme/context exceptions rather than a universal single-value assumption.

author: Sengsoulin, Bounleuth
title: Pali and Sanskrit words in Lao language
scope: Discusses Indic-origin vocabulary in Lao. Use as a separate lexical/orthographic profile lead; do not assign modern spoken-Lao IPA from etymological spellings alone.

author: Yanagimura, Y.
title: Contextual Tonal Variations in Vientiane Lao
scope: Studies all 25 bitonal sequences from five lexical tones in one Vientiane variety using recorded productions and F0 contours. Reports stronger carryover than anticipatory effects and context-dependent tonal realization. Published text can guide prosodic caution; this is not a grapheme-to-lexical-tone mapping table.

author: Lee, Jackson L. et al.
title: Massively Multilingual Pronunciation Modeling with WikiPron
scope: Wiktionary-derived pronunciation lexicon and G2P resource. Lao-specific coverage, source provenance, dialect and license need separate verification before use; generated or imported entries must not be assumed to be independently authored Lao IPA.

author: Wilson, Brian Eugene; Campbell, Robert Martin; with Arlyta Keosamone and Bualong Nyoukmai
title: Lao-Dictionary word list
scope: 77 KB Lao word list with BSD-style redistribution notice in its own header. The header says it was created for word wrapping and that compound words have mostly been reduced to their parts. It contains orthographic headwords, names and loan forms but no IPA; candidate segmentation hints only, not word-boundary gold or pronunciation data.
